prose.en: Tori breaks uke's balance toward the left rear corner, bends the right knee, places the back of the right knee against the back of uke's left knee from the inside, and reaps in an arc, as though drawing a semicircle, to throw uke.

Image of the technique and the ukemi (breakfall). In the last frame tori's grip on uke's sleeve is circled in red. Uke's cooperation: As the left leg is reaped, uke takes ushiro-ukemi (rear breakfall) supported on the right foot. Tori's cooperation: Tori pulls up on uke's right sleeve so that uke can take a solid ukemi. Tori, using a forward tai-sabaki (body movement), breaks uke's balance to the rear and throws by reaping the back of uke's left knee with the right leg.

heading.en: Introductory way of applying the technique

prose.en: Tori reaps uke, who is down on one knee, from the inside and throws.
When uke steps back, apply o-uchi-gari with a forward tai-sabaki.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: Tori should not let the reaping position become too high.
Do not fall together with uke. Tori stands firmly and pulls with the pulling hand (hikite). Uke does not cling to tori.
